title: Knowledge exception
description: A person's explicit, expiring acceptance that one rule of core/reference/lessons.yaml applicable to a run is not satisfied by it. Only a rule whose level the lessons file's `exceptions.levels` lists can be excepted (blocking and required: the others never block). `approved_by.mode` must be one the file's `exceptions.approvers` accepts for the rule's level - `human` (a person) for both as shipped; a blocking rule is a person's to except, never automation's (check-integrity refuses `automation` there). An exception is run-scoped: it is granted for one run as an operator act, never by configuration; it expires (at most `exceptions.max_days` after `created_at`), and one expired at the moment it is read counts as not granted. It never makes a rule satisfied: the rule is reported EXCEPTED, and the exception is listed wherever the rule's compliance is. The rules beyond this shape (rule exists, level, approver, window, expiry) are checked by scripts/wgf_knowledge/model.py exception_problems. See docs/knowledge-enforcement.md.

rule_id.description: The lesson id of core/reference/lessons.yaml the exception is for.

reason.description: Why the rule is accepted unmet for this run, in a person's words: what was seen, why it is acceptable now, and what will close it.

scope.description: What the exception covers within the run. Empty: every check of the rule on every targeted platform and viewport.

checks.description: Check ids of the rule (core/reference/check-tiers.yaml) it covers.

viewports.description: Viewport or project names it covers.

identifier.description: Who approved it: a person's handle or name.

mode.description: human: a person, from outside the run. automation: a decision made inside a Factory step's process tree - refused for every level as shipped, and always for a blocking rule.

expires_at.description: Mandatory. After it the exception does not hold.

run_id.description: The run it was granted in, when recorded outside the run's own events.
